title: Lease vs licence - a distinction that changes everything legally
p1:
Two people can use the same property, pay the same money, and still have completely different legal rights.

The reason? The agreement may be a lease or only a licence.
p2: Many assume that any permission to occupy a property creates a lease. That is not always true. A licence usually gives permission to use a space, while a lease creates a stronger legal interest in the property.
p3:
The difference can affect eviction rights, control over the property, and the level of protection available to the occupant. For example, calling an agreement a 'licence' does not automatically make it one—the actual terms and the nature of possession matter more than the label.

A small wording choice in a property agreement can create a major legal consequence later.
conclusion: Have you ever seen an agreement called a licence that actually looked more like a lease? What was your experience?
